- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.5–1.0), model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap upward correction after 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts drift far from recent 7–14 day average; pull forecast back toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); increase forecast by 1–2% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0 → +0.5), model tends to misread trend direction; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint.
